title: Fizz Buzz

concept.title: The order of the checks matters
body: A number divisible by both 3 and 5 satisfies *both* the "divisible by 3" test and the "divisible by 5" test. In an `if / else if` chain only the first true branch runs, so if you test "divisible by 3" first, 15 prints `Fizz` and never reaches the case that should print `FizzBuzz`.
The rule: put the most specific condition first. Here that is "divisible by 3 **and** 5" (or, equivalently, divisible by 15).
Whether `n` is divisible by `k` is the test `n % k == 0`.

list: `FizzBuzz` if `n` is divisible by both 3 and 5

hints: Which numbers are divisible by both 3 and 5? Which test describes them?
Check the "both" case first, then 3, then 5.
The last `else` prints the number itself.

explanation: Divisible by both 3 and 5 means divisible by 15, and that test must come first. After it, the remaining branches handle 3 and 5 on their own.
